name: Claude Reflect — Anthropic's AI Usage Analytics Dashboard; Free/Pro/Max Beta; 'Your Spotify Wrapped for Claude'
hook: Anthropic launched Reflect today — a built-in usage analytics dashboard that summarizes your Claude activity across 1, 3, 6, or 12-month windows and maps it to Anthropic's 4D AI Fluency Framework (delegation, description, discernment, diligence). It shows which topics you engage with most, identifies usage patterns, lets you set quiet hours and break nudges, and prompts you to flag tasks you'd rather keep doing yourself even when Claude could help. TechCrunch ran with 'quietly selling you on AI'; Digital Trends called it 'your usual Spotify Wrapped, but for Anthropic.' Beta for Free, Pro, and Max users with Memory enabled, via Settings on web and desktop. A parallel Enterprise update brings the admin analytics dashboard to group- and user-level cost breakdowns with artifacts created, files edited, and skills/connectors used listed alongside their costs.

name: Claude Cowork Expands to Mobile and Web — Background Cloud Execution, iOS/Android/Web, Microsoft 365 Write Tools; Doubled Limits Through Aug 5
hook: Cowork, which launched as a desktop app in January, landed on iOS, Android, and claude.ai web on July 7 — and the key upgrade is cloud execution: tasks now run on Anthropic infrastructure rather than requiring your laptop to stay on. Start work on your desktop, get a push notification when Claude needs approval, pick up the finished output on your phone hours later. New Microsoft 365 write tools let Claude draft and send email, manage calendar events, and create or update OneDrive and SharePoint files. Chat and Cowork share a unified sidebar on web and desktop. VentureBeat's headline: 'most users aren't coding' — the data justifies the pivot from developer tool to all-day AI coworker. Anthropic is extending doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5.

name: Alibaba Bans Claude Code for All Employees — BAN EFFECTIVE TOMORROW (July 10); Staff Redirected to Qoder
hook: Alibaba's company-wide Claude Code ban takes effect tomorrow, July 10 — the direct consequence of the steganographic tracking code incident. Employees are directed to Qoder. The underlying conflict: on June 10 Anthropic told the US Senate Banking Committee that Alibaba's Qwen lab ran the largest known Claude distillation attack (~28.8M exchanges via 25,000 fraudulent accounts). Alibaba denied it. Anthropic then embedded timezone/proxy-hostname signals in hidden Unicode in Claude Code v2.1.91–v2.1.196. LegitMichel777 and Thereallo exposed it on June 30; fix shipped in v2.1.197. The ban is covered by SCMP, Tom's Hardware, TechCrunch, TechRadar, The Next Web, and BankInfoSecurity.
